      "title": "Authorization OR fragment can be returned without enclosing parentheses",
      "body": "buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition may produce SQL shaped like (A) OR (B), but getBaseConditions returns authConditions unchanged when there is no filter condition. If a caller composes this fragment with additional predicates, for example WHERE ${baseConditions} AND another_condition, SQL precedence makes the added predicate apply only to the last OR branch, potentially returning rows outside the authorized set. The exposed condition should always be wrapped in parentheses, or the builders should return parenthesized fragments."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts",

      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Org scope excludes direct org members' individual bookings when there are no child teams",
      "body": "buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only fetches member user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. If an organization has no child teams, teamIds still contains the org ID and direct org memberships can exist, but the generated condition only matches team bookings (teamId = ANY([orgId]) AND isTeamBooking = true). Individual bookings of org members (isTeamBooking = false) are omitted. Memberships should be fetched for [orgId, ...childTeamIds] regardless of whether child teams exist."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts",
      "line": 159,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Member enumeration for raw authorization does not explicitly filter accepted memberships",
      "body": "isOrgOwnerOrAdmin checks membership.accepted, but buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition call MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds without an accepted filter. If that repository method can return pending or invited memberships, their user IDs are included in the userId = ANY(...) condition and their individual bookings become visible in org/team insights. Add an explicit accepted filter or ensure the repository guarantees it."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts",
      "line": 332,

      "title": "Org-scope expectation depends on unspecified ordering of repository results",
      "body": "The test expects exact arrays inside ANY(...) in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds without explicit ordering. If the database returns teams or memberships in a different order, the Prisma.sql values differ and the test fails even though the SQL is semantically the same. Sort IDs deterministically in the service or make the assertion order-independent."
    },

The org/team authorization conditions that use = ANY(${array}) are only compared as Prisma.sql objects and never run against the database. This leaves array parameter binding and the actual row-filtering behavior of the high-risk org/team scopes unverified. Add integration tests that execute org/team base conditions and assert included and excluded rows."
    },

findings.title: Authorization OR fragment can be returned without enclosing parentheses
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition may produce SQL shaped like (A) OR (B), but getBaseConditions returns authConditions unchanged when there is no filter condition. If a caller composes this fragment with additional predicates, for example WHERE ${baseConditions} AND another_condition, SQL precedence makes the added predicate apply only to the last OR branch, potentially returning rows outside the authorized set. The exposed condition should always be wrapped in parentheses, or the builders should return parenthesized fragments.

findings.title: Org scope excludes direct org members' individual bookings when there are no child teams
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only fetches member user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. If an organization has no child teams, teamIds still contains the org ID and direct org memberships can exist, but the generated condition only matches team bookings (teamId = ANY([orgId]) AND isTeamBooking = true). Individual bookings of org members (isTeamBooking = false) are omitted. Memberships should be fetched for [orgId, ...childTeamIds] regardless of whether child teams exist.

findings.title: Member enumeration for raw authorization does not explicitly filter accepted memberships
findings.body: isOrgOwnerOrAdmin checks membership.accepted, but buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition call MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds without an accepted filter. If that repository method can return pending or invited memberships, their user IDs are included in the userId = ANY(...) condition and their individual bookings become visible in org/team insights. Add an explicit accepted filter or ensure the repository guarantees it.

findings.title: Org-scope expectation depends on unspecified ordering of repository results
findings.body: The test expects exact arrays inside ANY(...) in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds without explicit ordering. If the database returns teams or memberships in a different order, the Prisma.sql values differ and the test fails even though the SQL is semantically the same. Sort IDs deterministically in the service or make the assertion order-independent.

findings.title: No integration test executes the org/team ANY raw SQL paths
findings.body: The only $queryRaw integration test uses user scope, which generates simple equality predicates. The org/team authorization conditions that use = ANY(${array}) are only compared as Prisma.sql objects and never run against the database. This leaves array parameter binding and the actual row-filtering behavior of the high-risk org/team scopes unverified. Add integration tests that execute org/team base conditions and assert included and excluded rows.

findings.title: Public findMany API removed without replacement or caller updates
findings.body: The diff deletes findMany and changes the public condition methods from returning Prisma where-input objects to returning raw Prisma.Sql fragments. Any existing caller that used InsightsBookingService.findMany or composed the old where objects will break. Since no consumer files are updated in this PR, confirm the service is unused elsewhere or update callers or provide a compatibility adapter before merging.
